review_text: BambooHR has been a game-changer for our small HR team. The employee self-service portal saves us hours every week. Onboarding new hires is seamless now.
The UI is clean and intuitive but the reporting module is severely lacking. We can't build custom reports without exporting to Excel first. For the price we pay this is unacceptable.
Solid HRIS for mid-market companies. Time-off tracking and org charts work great. We switched from spreadsheets and the difference is night and day.
BambooHR's customer support has gone downhill. Response times went from hours to days. We're actively evaluating Rippling as a replacement.
We love the applicant tracking system integration. However the performance reviews module feels like an afterthought compared to dedicated performance platforms.
Perfect for companies under 200 employees. Once we crossed that threshold the system started showing its limitations in workflow automation and approvals.
BambooHR's mobile app is excellent. Our field employees can request PTO and view pay stubs without calling HR. Implementation took only 3 weeks.
The benefits administration module is too basic. We had to keep our separate benefits broker portal running alongside BambooHR which defeats the purpose.
We evaluated BambooHR Workday and Rippling. BambooHR won on ease of use but we worry about outgrowing it. The analytics dashboard needs serious improvement.
Great for core HR but lacks the payroll depth we need. We run BambooHR alongside Gusto for payroll which is redundant and expensive.
The document management and e-signatures are solid. Employee satisfaction surveys are a nice bonus. Would give 5 stars but the API is limited.
BambooHR keeps raising prices without adding proportional value. We're paying 40% more than 2 years ago and the product hasn't changed much.
Onboarding workflows are the best feature. New hire paperwork that used to take 3 days now happens before day one. The preboarding experience is excellent.
Simple and reliable for a 75-person company. Not flashy but it gets the job done. The employee directory with org chart is everyone's favorite feature.
After 3 years on BambooHR we're migrating to Workday. BambooHR can't handle our multi-entity multi-currency needs as we expanded internationally.
The training tracking feature is underrated. We use it for compliance certifications and it's saved us from multiple audit headaches.
BambooHR's ATS is decent for small companies but falls apart with high-volume recruiting. We do 50+ hires per month and the pipeline management can't keep up.
Love the culture features - employee recognition and satisfaction scores. These help us stay ahead of engagement issues before they become attrition problems.
The integration marketplace is growing but still missing some key connectors. We need native Slack and Microsoft Teams integration not just Zapier workarounds.
BambooHR handles our core HR needs well but I wish they invested more in analytics. Compared to what Workday offers in people analytics BambooHR feels a generation behind.
We use BambooHR for PTO tracking and it's flawless. The calendar view showing team availability has reduced scheduling conflicts dramatically.
Implementation was smooth but data migration from our old system took longer than promised. Once running the day-to-day experience is great.
Decent mid-market HRIS. Not trying to be everything to everyone which is refreshing. Focus on core HR and they do it well.
BambooHR's employee self-service reduced HR tickets by 60%. Staff can update their own info access documents and request time off independently.
The pricing model is confusing. Per-employee costs add up fast and some features we consider basic are only in the higher tier.
BambooHR does what it promises. No surprises no hidden complexity. For a 120-person company this is exactly the right tool.
We needed more advanced compensation management and BambooHR fell short. The comp planning tools are too simplistic for our leveling framework.
BambooHR's customer success team during implementation was fantastic. They helped us configure everything and train our team. Post-implementation support is another story.
We run BambooHR for 85 employees across 3 offices. The centralized employee database with role-based access is exactly what we needed to replace our Google Sheets mess.
Adequate but uninspiring. BambooHR does the basics fine but hasn't innovated in years. Meanwhile competitors like Rippling are leapfrogging them with automation features.
Workday HCM transformed how we manage our 5000-person workforce. The unified finance and HR data model is powerful for strategic planning and headcount budgeting.
Workday is incredibly powerful but the implementation was an 18-month nightmare. Budget overran by 200% and we needed 3 dedicated consultants the entire time.
The reporting and analytics in Workday are best-in-class. People analytics dashboards give us insights we never had before. Worth the complexity for large enterprises.
We spent $2M implementing Workday and our end users still prefer the old system. The UI is not intuitive for non-HR employees. Training costs are ongoing.
Workday Recruiting is solid but not as specialized as Greenhouse or Lever. If recruiting is your priority you might want a best-of-breed ATS alongside Workday.
The Workday mobile experience is surprisingly good. Managers can approve requests review team data and run basic reports from their phones.
Workday's security model is enterprise-grade. SOC 2 compliance role-based access and audit trails give us confidence for our regulated industry.
For a company our size (300 employees) Workday is overkill. We're paying enterprise prices for features we'll never use. Should have gone with BambooHR or Rippling.
The Workday Community forums and documentation are excellent. When we hit issues the community usually has the answer before support responds.
Workday Adaptive Planning integration with HCM is a game-changer for headcount planning and financial forecasting. No other platform does this as seamlessly.
The bi-annual Workday updates break our custom configurations every time. We spend 6 weeks testing and fixing after each release. It's exhausting.
Compensation management in Workday is comprehensive. Merit cycles bonus calculations and equity management all in one place with full audit trail.
Workday's learning management module (Workday Learning) is mediocre compared to dedicated LMS platforms. We still run Cornerstone alongside it.
If you have 1000+ employees and need a unified HCM+Finance platform Workday is the gold standard. For smaller orgs look elsewhere.
Workday Prism Analytics gave us the ability to combine external benchmark data with internal HR metrics. Our board presentations have never been more data-driven.
We switched to Workday from SAP SuccessFactors. Better user experience but the migration was painful. Six months in we're happy with the decision.
The Workday talent marketplace and career pathing features are helping us with internal mobility. Employees can see growth opportunities across the organization.
Workday's time tracking module doesn't handle complex shift patterns well. Our manufacturing teams need something more specialized for schedule management.
The Total Rewards statement in Workday is fantastic for employee retention. People can see their complete compensation picture including benefits equity and bonuses.
Workday pricing is opaque and negotiations are difficult. Be prepared to pay consultant rates on top of licensing for any customization.
We use Workday for 3200 employees across 12 countries. The localization and compliance features for international payroll are unmatched.
After evaluating Workday and UKG we chose Workday for its superior analytics. Three years later no regrets despite the higher total cost of ownership.
Workday's succession planning tools helped us identify and develop our next generation of leaders. The 9-box grid with integrated talent data is very useful.
The Workday integration cloud (Studio) is powerful but requires developer-level skills. Not something an HR admin can configure without IT support.
Workday Peakon for engagement surveys integrates beautifully with the core HCM. Real-time pulse surveys with action planning built right into the manager dashboard.
Honestly Workday is the enterprise HR platform that does everything adequately but nothing exceptionally. Jack of all trades master of none.
For our global org the multi-currency multi-language support in Workday was essential. No other vendor could match the depth of localization.
Workday performance management lets us run continuous feedback 360 reviews and goal alignment all in one place. Managers actually use it which says a lot.
We're trapped in Workday. The switching costs are astronomical once you're in. They know this and price renewals accordingly.
Workday's absence management handles our complex PTO policies across states and countries. The accrual engine is highly configurable.
Rippling is the most innovative HR platform we've evaluated. The unified employee system that connects HR IT and Finance is years ahead of the competition.
We switched from BambooHR to Rippling and the difference in automation is staggering. What took our HR team hours now happens automatically.
Rippling's device management alongside HR is genius. Onboarding a new employee means their laptop apps and access are all provisioned automatically.
The platform is fast-moving which is both good and bad. New features constantly but sometimes they feel half-baked. The benefits module launched with bugs.
Rippling's global payroll covers 50+ countries. We consolidated three separate payroll vendors into one platform. The cost savings alone justified the switch.
For a tech company Rippling feels like it was built by people who understand our needs. The Slack integration automatic software provisioning and IT automation are unmatched.
Rippling's customer support is hit or miss. When you get a good rep things move fast. But our dedicated CSM changed three times in one year.
The expense management module is a nice addition. Employees submit receipts through the app and reimbursements flow through payroll automatically.
We evaluated Rippling against Gusto for our 50-person startup. Rippling won on automation and IT management. Gusto was cheaper but more manual.
Rippling's workflow automations are incredible. We built custom triggers for everything from compliance reminders to equipment ordering when someone changes roles.
The learning management system in Rippling is basic. We need something more robust for our compliance training requirements in healthcare.
Rippling's app management changed our IT game. When we offboard someone their access to all 30+ SaaS tools is revoked instantly. Security team loves it.
The headcount planning features in Rippling are surprisingly good for a platform that's not primarily HCM. Better than what BambooHR offers by far.
Rippling's implementation was fast - 4 weeks from kickoff to go-live for 200 employees. The data migration tools imported everything from our old HRIS cleanly.
The analytics and reporting are getting better but still behind Workday. For quick operational reports it's fine. For deep people analytics we supplement with Visier.
Rippling handles our multi-state payroll flawlessly. Tax filing compliance and W-2 generation are all automated. Saved us from needing a payroll specialist.
The time and attendance module needs work. Our hourly employees find the clock-in process clunky compared to dedicated time tracking tools.
We love that Rippling unifies identity management with HR. SSO SCIM and directory services built into the same platform as payroll and benefits.
Rippling's PEO option was perfect for us before we were big enough for our own benefits. Seamless transition from PEO to our own plans as we grew.
Price went up significantly at renewal. They hook you with reasonable initial pricing then increase substantially. Still worth it for the automation though.
Rippling's compound system approach means every new module they add benefits from shared data. The inventory management for company devices integrates with onboarding beautifully.
We have 350 employees and Rippling scales well. The org chart workflow approvals and compensation bands all work smoothly at our size.
Migrated from ADP to Rippling. The modern interface and automation capabilities make ADP feel like it was built in 2005. Our team is much happier.
Rippling's custom fields and workflows give us flexibility no other HRIS offers. We've built processes specific to our industry without any coding.
Performance reviews in Rippling are decent but not as mature as Lattice or 15Five. For a company focused on performance culture you'll want a dedicated tool.
The Rippling Unity platform is impressive conceptually. Having HR IT and Finance share the same employee graph means less data sync and fewer errors.
Some features feel rushed to market. The recruiting module launched without basic interview scheduling capabilities. They fixed it but first impressions matter.
Rippling's insurance broker integration is smooth. Benefits enrollment was the easiest we've ever run. Employees completed it in under 10 minutes each.
I worry about Rippling trying to do too much too fast. They're expanding into spend management and inventory. Focus on perfecting HR first.
Rippling's API is well-documented and responsive. We built custom integrations with our internal tools in days not weeks. Developer experience is excellent.
Gusto is perfect for our 25-person startup. Payroll taxes benefits - all handled beautifully. The interface is so simple even our non-technical founders run payroll.
We outgrew Gusto around 80 employees. The lack of advanced workflows approval chains and custom permissions became a bottleneck. Moving to Rippling.
Gusto's payroll is absolutely flawless. Never had an error in 3 years. Tax filings are automatic and year-end W-2s are ready ahead of schedule.
For the price Gusto is unbeatable for small businesses. We pay $40/mo base plus $6 per employee. The ROI compared to manual payroll processing is massive.
Gusto's health insurance marketplace integration is great for small companies. We got competitive rates that we couldn't have accessed independently.
The Gusto Wallet feature for employees is a nice perk. Cash advances against earned wages help our hourly workers with cash flow.
Gusto's contractor payment handling is excellent. We have 20 contractors and managing their 1099s and payments is seamless. International contractor support was recently added.
The HR features beyond payroll feel bolted on. Document storage org charts and onboarding are basic compared to BambooHR or Rippling.
Gusto's team communication features are lacking. No built-in announcements or company news feed. We use Slack for everything that Gusto should handle internally.
For a simple clean payroll solution Gusto is my top recommendation. We switched from ADP and cut our payroll processing time by 75%.
Gusto's customer support is responsive and helpful. Live chat gets answers in minutes not hours. They genuinely seem to care about small businesses.
The performance review tools are extremely basic. Just a simple form with no calibration 9-box or development planning. Not suitable for companies focused on talent development.
Gusto's time tracking integration with payroll is great. Employees clock in through the app and hours flow directly into payroll calculation. Zero manual entry.
We tried using Gusto as our full HRIS and it's just not designed for that. It's a payroll platform with HR features not an HR platform with payroll.
The state tax registration service saved us weeks of paperwork when we hired remote employees in new states. Gusto handles the filings automatically.
Gusto's benefits administration for small groups is surprisingly comprehensive. Dental vision 401k HSA - all managed in one place.
No multi-entity support is a dealbreaker for our holding company structure. We need separate EINs and Gusto forces everything into one entity.
The employee self-service portal is clean and easy to use. Pay stubs tax documents and benefits info are all accessible. Employees rarely ask HR for this info anymore.
Gusto recently added workforce costing reports which is helpful for budgeting. Still not as robust as what Workday offers but impressive for the price point.
The onboarding checklist in Gusto is functional but inflexible. Can't customize the flow based on department or role. Everyone gets the same generic experience.
Gusto's compliance alerts are a lifesaver for small businesses without dedicated HR. They flag upcoming deadlines and regulatory changes proactively.
Integration options are limited compared to larger platforms. We need a native integration with our recruiting tool and Gusto only offers it through a third-party connector.
For companies in California Gusto handles the complex state requirements expertly. Multi-jurisdiction tax withholding and reporting just works.
The Gusto Plus plan has everything a 30-person company needs. We've been happy customers for 2 years with zero plans to switch.
Gusto's new hiring and onboarding tools are getting better but still can't compete with dedicated platforms. Fine for 5 hires per month - not for 50.
I love the simplicity. Other platforms try to be everything. Gusto does payroll and benefits exceptionally well and that's what we need.
We compared Gusto with Namely for our 60-person company. Gusto won on payroll ease. Namely won on HR depth. Went with Gusto and supplement with other tools.
The API is limited for custom integrations. We needed to push employee data to our learning platform and Gusto's API couldn't handle the custom fields.
Gusto handles garnishments and deductions correctly every single time. For a company with lots of court-ordered deductions this reliability is critical.
Solid payroll platform that's growing into more. Not there yet as a full HRIS but the trajectory is promising. Keep an eye on Gusto if you're a small company.
Namely promised us an all-in-one HR platform for mid-market and largely delivers. Payroll HR benefits and talent management in one system for our 250-person company.
The implementation experience was rocky. Namely's team seemed understaffed and our project timeline slipped by 2 months. Once live the platform works well though.
Namely's social news feed and company directory make it feel like a modern workplace tool not just boring HR software. Employee adoption has been excellent.
Performance management in Namely is good enough. Goal tracking continuous feedback and annual reviews all in one place. Not best-in-class but integrated which matters.
We've had recurring payroll calculation errors that took months to resolve. For a payroll platform this is the one thing that absolutely must work perfectly.
Namely's benefits administration and open enrollment management are strong. The employee-facing benefits comparison tool helps people make informed choices.
The platform feels dated compared to Rippling. Navigation is clunky and some pages take 5+ seconds to load. A UI refresh is overdue.
Namely handles our multi-state payroll well for a mid-market platform. Not as robust as Workday but we don't need Workday's complexity or price tag.
The customizable workflows for onboarding offboarding and role changes are one of Namely's best features. We've automated most of our HR processes.
Namely's reporting engine improved significantly in the last year. Custom report builder with scheduling and automated distribution. Finally competitive with other platforms.
Customer support response times are inconsistent. Sometimes we get same-day resolution sometimes tickets sit for a week. No clear escalation path.
We switched from Namely to BambooHR for simplicity. Namely had too many features we didn't use and the complexity wasn't worth it for our 80-person team.
Namely's managed payroll service takes the burden off our small HR team. They handle the complex calculations and filings while we focus on people.
The time and attendance module is functional but basic. For companies with complex shift scheduling or project-based time tracking you'll want a supplement.
Namely's HRIS core is solid for mid-market. Employee records document management and organizational structure are all well-designed and easy to maintain.
We evaluated Namely Gusto and Rippling for our 150-person company. Namely offered the best balance of functionality and price for our specific needs.
The ACA compliance reporting in Namely saved us from significant penalties. Automatic 1094-C and 1095-C generation with real-time eligibility tracking.
Namely's mobile app needs serious improvement. Half the features available on desktop aren't accessible on mobile. Remote workers find this frustrating.
The employee self-service in Namely is comprehensive. PTO requests benefits changes personal info updates - all handled without HR intervention.
Namely acquired a learning management platform and the integration shows. The LMS feels disconnected from the core HR platform. Poor data sync between modules.
We're a 200-employee nonprofit and Namely gave us nonprofit pricing. The platform handles our grant-funded position tracking and allocation reporting.
Namely's compensation management tools are adequate. Not as powerful as dedicated comp platforms but having it integrated with the HRIS is convenient.
The survey and engagement tools in Namely are a recent addition and it shows. Basic pulse surveys without the analytics depth that Culture Amp or Lattice offer.
API documentation is decent but the API itself has rate limiting issues. Our integration with Okta occasionally fails during large directory syncs.
For mid-market companies that want one platform for everything Namely is a reasonable choice. Not the cheapest not the best at anything but solid across the board.
Namely's open enrollment experience for employees is the best we've seen. Side-by-side plan comparison cost calculators and dependent management all in one flow.
We were early Namely customers and the platform has matured significantly. Early bugs and reliability issues are mostly resolved. Much more stable now.
Namely's org chart visualization is one of the best I've used. Interactive filterable and always up-to-date with real HR data.
The talent acquisition module in Namely is too basic for serious recruiting operations. We still need Greenhouse for our interview pipeline management.
Namely does a good job bridging the gap between small-company tools like Gusto and enterprise platforms like Workday. Perfect for the 150-500 employee sweet spot.
